profile.reading:
This point is mapped as NTT Ashburn VA9 at 44710 Gigabit Plaza, Ashburn, VA 20147, on the same Gigabit Plaza cluster as NTT's confirmed VA3, VA6, VA7, and VA8 buildings. NTT does not publish a dedicated facility page for VA9, and its own campus index and overview pages list only VA1, VA2, VA3, VA4, VA5, VA7, and VA11 as named, page-linked buildings; VA9 does not appear at all in NTT's own public materials, though the address itself comes from public geocoded property data placing a real structure at that location. This entry does not assert a square footage or MW figure it cannot confirm from NTT's own site. NTT describes its overall Ashburn campus as 224 megawatts of critical IT load across 78 acres in Loudoun County's "Data Center Alley," a figure that necessarily includes whatever capacity VA9 contributes, even though NTT does not break that figure out by building for every address on the campus.

Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Ashburn-area facility. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates that will raise a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers effective January 1, 2027, under which large-demand campus buildings like this one face 14-year mandatory contracts and minimum cost-coverage requirements, per Inside Climate News's reporting on the SCC decision. NTT's individually documented Ashburn buildings offer a scale reference for a typical building on this campus: VA1, a few blocks away at 44664 Guilford Drive, is confirmed by NTT's own site at 64,723 square feet of raised floor and 12.6 megawatts of critical IT load, though this registry does not apply VA1's specific figures to VA9 since NTT has not confirmed the two buildings match. NTT's own building numbering on this campus runs at least through VA11, and several numbers, including this one, currently lack an individually published facility page despite OSM survey data placing a real, named structure at the mapped address.

reading.body:
NTT Ashburn VA9 is one of 326 mapped data center facilities in Virginia, but its power capacity is not published. Of the 23 Virginia facilities with published specifications, this campus ranks 24th, placing it outside the published tier. Without a disclosed megawatt figure, its contribution to Virginia's 1375.4 MW of published data center capacity cannot be quantified.

The facility sits on Gigabit Plaza in Ashburn, the core of Northern Virginia's data center cluster. Ashburn hosts the densest concentration of large data centers in the United States, drawn by proximity to internet exchanges, fiber routes, and the aging but still-functional regional grid. A campus at this address with no published power spec is either smaller than the threshold operators typically disclose, or operates under a confidentiality restriction common in the region.

Without power capacity, racks, or tenant information in the published record, this facility's relevance to AI scaling cannot be read from available data. NTT operates a global data center portfolio and has made acquisitions in Europe, but no specific investments in US AI infrastructure are stated here. Researchers tracking AI infrastructure growth should flag this site for future disclosure or treat it as part of Virginia's unmeasured capacity reserve.
